chunks: Abu al-Jarud narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
That the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said to 'Ali عليه السلام: “Indeed, I love for you what I love for myself, and I dislike for you what I dislike for myself.

So do not wear a gold ring, for it is your adornment in the Hereafter; and do not wear crimson, for it is among the garments of Iblis; and do not ride on a red saddlecloth, for it is among the mounts of Iblis; and do not wear silk, lest Allah burn your skin on the Day you meet Him.”

key_terms.مِيثَرَةٍ حَمْرَاءَ: a red saddlecloth or cushion used for riding

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbid Imam 'Ali عليه السلام from wearing or riding?
ai.summary: This hadith reports the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instruction to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام regarding forms of adornment and dress that are forbidden or disliked. It combines affectionate counsel with legal and moral warning, linking certain worldly adornments to the Hereafter and to blameworthy imitation.
